Vengeance Demon Hunter Rotation in 

Vengeance Demon Hunters operate on a priority list builder-spender system. Depending on the situation, you will prioritize either building or spending one of our two resources while trying to avoid overcapping either of them. You generally want to abide by the following rules:

 

 

 
 Generators are key: While in most cases there is a fairly smooth flow between building and spending, whenever there is a priority conflict, it is more important to keep your generators on cooldown due to procs associated with Fracture and Soul Fragment generation for the Hero trees. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Prioritize Spenders by Soul cost: You should always try to use Soul spenders with as many Souls as possible. This gives the maximum efficiency per global used.
 

 

 
 

 
 Avoid Overcapping Resources when Possible: While it is sometimes inevitable due to multiple generators coming off cooldown and priority conflict, try to build and spend in waves to manage resources. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Press Cooldowns as they become Available: Maximize cooldown efficiency by constantly using abilities as they become available. Procs can get wasted if your abilities are sitting off cooldown for long periods. 
 

 

Vengeance Demon Hunter Starter Guide

Best Vengeance Demon Hunter Opener

Our opener is generally fairly set, with minor variations depending on the type of pull. Generally, the rule is to get all of our cooldowns rolling in a sequence to avoid any potential waste or missed casts. Following that, after everything is set up, we transition smoothly into our buff management and ability cycling, and as such we are less reliant on opener damage overall. It's instead a way to hit the ground running. Pre-Combat Check

Before any combat happens, it is important for Vengeance Demon Hunters to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Vengeance Demon Hunter Major Cooldowns

Offensive Cooldowns

Using Offensive Cooldowns as they become available is generally the best option.
 

 Spell 
 Cooldown 
 When to use 

 Fel Devastation 
 40 seconds (28-34 seconds with Darkglare Boon ) 
 Generally on cooldown. If you have Fiery Demise and Down in Flames , sync it with one cast of Fiery Brand . 

 Soul Carver 
 1 minute 
 On cooldown, with fewer than 3 souls. If you have Fiery Demise talented, sync it with Fiery Brand . 

 Sigil of Spite 
 1 minute 
 On cooldown, ideally synced with Fiery Brand if talented into Fiery Demise . 

 

Defensive Cooldowns

None of our defensive cooldowns are particularly powerful, so in general we recommend maximizing usage by using them as they become available. If you aren't actively Tanking, you can hold for a short period.
 

 Spell 
 Cooldown 
 When to use 

 Metamorphosis 
 2 minutes, reduced by some talents 
 On cooldown, but not if you are already in Metamorphosis from another proc and it has more than 5 seconds remaining, as it will overwrite the duration instead of extending. 

 Fel Devastation 
 40 seconds (28-34 seconds with Darkglare Boon ) 
 Generally on cooldown when you are below 70% health. If you have Fiery Demise and Down in Flames , sync it with one cast of Fiery Brand . 

 Fiery Brand 
 1 minute (48 seconds with Down in Flames ) 
 On cooldown. If you have a large tankbuster coming soon, you can hold it for up to 10 seconds. If running Down in Flames , sync one charge with offensive cooldowns. 

 Demon Spikes 
 20 seconds (reduced by haste) 
 Whenever you do not have any other defensives active, or if your charges would fully recharge before any other active defensives run out. 

 Darkness 
 5 minutes (3 with Pitch Black ) 
 On cooldown as much as possible. Hold for any group damage phases, especially if there are multiple hits, or pulls with many adds. 

 

 Vengeance Demon Hunter Advanced Tips

There is very little optimization for Vengeance after the Midnight pruning.

 
 Fracture 

 Fracture optimization is a minor optimization that can be managed when playing . When you are at full stacks of Voidfall or in the process of spending them, avoid pressing Fracture since you cannot generate. That means you want to prioritize it more heavily when you are about to proc the third stack.

Our Vengeance Demon Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Vengeance Demon Hunter guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page, along with our list of Related Guides just beneath the Table of Contents .

 Builder Priority is Fracture at 2 stacks ➜ Immolation Aura ➜ Sigil of Flame ➜ Sigil of Spite .

 Spender Priority is Spirit Bomb with 6 Souls ➜ Soul Cleave with 1-3 Souls ➜ Fel Devastation ➜ Soul Cleave with 0 Souls.

While builders tend to take priority, spenders are important for a smooth rotation. Try to weave them in to prevent overcapping resources.

You want to be pressing something every GCD, and abilities with cooldowns are more efficient.

Comment by Horsekebab 
One thing that I've been trying to find information about, is the balancing between using soul cleave for damage and for healing. This guide seems to straight out ignore the fact that if you use soul cleave at max hp and >1 souls, those souls are straight out wasted, suggesting that it's not very important to properly time the consumption of souls. Is that really so?

I've been comparing soul cleave to DK's death strike (DK main), but perhaps that's the wrong way to look at it. After all, soul cleave is a huge portion of Vengeance's AoE damage, and the trade-off for pooling souls will lead to a lot fewer soul cleave casts. In contrast, a DK can pool runic power to sit on 1 death strike always ready, and another death strike after one more GCD of RP-generation, without ever wasting any RP at all. They can of course also choose to pool 3 death strikes at a DPS loss, but much less significant (at least in multi-target situations) than DH's equivalent of sitting at 5 souls, especially now with set bonus and heart strike spam.

On top of it all, without borrowed power, DH's AoE damage without soul cleave is just not enough to keep up with threat generation during the burst of many classes, which rules out pooling souls during big pulls, which is exactly when reactive self-healing is needed the most.

I don't see any option but to accept that souls don't really comprise a reactive gameplay element, and the ability to self-heal is based on being lucky with the timing of incoming damage. Are Vengeance players happy with the design of souls and soul cleave?
